name: Exploding skull
summary: A CT-scanned adult human skull (WitmerLab specimen OUVC 10503) segmented into its individual bones, like a classic Beauchene 'exploded skull'. Separate the parts to see the 8 cranial bones of the braincase, the facial bones, the mandible and both dental arches, and how each bone meets its neighbours.
clinical: The thin H-shaped junction of the frontal, parietal, sphenoid (greater wing) and temporal bones on the side of the skull. The anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery runs deep to it, so a blow here can tear the artery and cause an extradural haematoma.
A fracture through the ethmoid's cribriform plate can tear the dura, causing CSF rhinorrhoea and loss of smell and opening a route for meningitis; periorbital bruising (raccoon eyes) is typical.

Cranium/Frontal.name: Frontal bone
Cranium/Frontal.description: Forms the forehead, the roofs of the orbits and most of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa. It contains the frontal sinuses and meets the two parietal bones at the coronal suture.

Cranium/Right Parietal.name: Right parietal bone
Cranium/Right Parietal.description: One of the paired bones forming most of the roof and side walls of the cranial vault. The parietals meet each other at the sagittal suture, the frontal at the coronal suture and the occipital at the lambdoid suture; branches of the middle meningeal artery groove the inner surface.

Cranium/Left parietal.name: Left parietal bone
Cranium/Left parietal.description: One of the paired bones forming most of the roof and side walls of the cranial vault. The parietals meet each other at the sagittal suture, the frontal at the coronal suture and the occipital at the lambdoid suture; branches of the middle meningeal artery groove the inner surface.

Cranium/Occipital.name: Occipital bone
Cranium/Occipital.description: Forms the back and much of the base of the skull around the foramen magnum, through which the brainstem becomes the spinal cord. Its occipital condyles articulate with the atlas (atlanto-occipital joint, the 'yes' nodding joint).

Cranium/Right temporal.name: Right temporal bone
Cranium/Right temporal.description: Forms the lower side wall and part of the base of the skull. Its dense petrous part houses the middle and inner ear; it also carries the external acoustic meatus, mastoid and styloid processes, the zygomatic process of the cheek arch and the mandibular fossa of the jaw joint (TMJ).

Cranium/Left temporal.name: Left temporal bone
Cranium/Left temporal.description: Forms the lower side wall and part of the base of the skull. Its dense petrous part houses the middle and inner ear; it also carries the external acoustic meatus, mastoid and styloid processes, the zygomatic process of the cheek arch and the mandibular fossa of the jaw joint (TMJ).

Cranium/Sphenoid.name: Sphenoid bone
Cranium/Sphenoid.description: The butterfly-shaped keystone of the cranial base, with a central body, greater and lesser wings and downward pterygoid processes. The body holds the sphenoid sinus and the sella turcica for the pituitary gland; the optic canal and the foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum pass through it.

Cranium/Ethmoid.name: Ethmoid bone
Cranium/Ethmoid.description: A light, air-filled bone between the orbits. Its cribriform plate transmits the olfactory nerve fibres, its perpendicular plate forms the upper nasal septum, and its labyrinths hold the ethmoidal air cells and bear the superior and middle nasal conchae.

Cranium/Right max.name: Right maxilla
Cranium/Right max.description: One of the paired bones of the upper jaw. It forms most of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, holds the upper teeth in its alveolar process and contains the maxillary sinus, the largest paranasal sinus.

Cranium/Left maxilla.name: Left maxilla
Cranium/Left maxilla.description: One of the paired bones of the upper jaw. It forms most of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, holds the upper teeth in its alveolar process and contains the maxillary sinus, the largest paranasal sinus.

Cranium/Right zygomatic.name: Right zygomatic bone
Cranium/Right zygomatic.description: The cheekbone, forming the prominence of the cheek and part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit. Its temporal process joins the zygomatic process of the temporal bone to make the zygomatic arch.

Cranium/Left zygomatic.name: Left zygomatic bone
Cranium/Left zygomatic.description: The cheekbone, forming the prominence of the cheek and part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit. Its temporal process joins the zygomatic process of the temporal bone to make the zygomatic arch.

Cranium/Right nasal.name: Right nasal bone
Cranium/Right nasal.description: One of two small oblong bones that meet in the midline to form the bony bridge of the nose, below the frontal bone. The nasal bones are the most commonly fractured bones of the face.

Cranium/Left nasal.name: Left nasal bone
Cranium/Left nasal.description: One of two small oblong bones that meet in the midline to form the bony bridge of the nose, below the frontal bone. The nasal bones are the most commonly fractured bones of the face.

Cranium/Right lacrimal.name: Right lacrimal bone
Cranium/Right lacrimal.description: A small, fragile plate in the front of the medial wall of the orbit. With the frontal process of the maxilla it forms the fossa for the lacrimal sac, which drains tears down the nasolacrimal canal into the nose.

Cranium/Left lacrimal.name: Left lacrimal bone
Cranium/Left lacrimal.description: A small, fragile plate in the front of the medial wall of the orbit. With the frontal process of the maxilla it forms the fossa for the lacrimal sac, which drains tears down the nasolacrimal canal into the nose.

Cranium/Right palatine.name: Right palatine bone
Cranium/Right palatine.description: An L-shaped bone behind the maxilla. Its horizontal plate forms the back third of the hard palate and its perpendicular plate part of the lateral nasal wall; the greater palatine foramen transmits the nerves and vessels of the palate.

Cranium/Left palatine.name: Left palatine bone
Cranium/Left palatine.description: An L-shaped bone behind the maxilla. Its horizontal plate forms the back third of the hard palate and its perpendicular plate part of the lateral nasal wall; the greater palatine foramen transmits the nerves and vessels of the palate.

Cranium/Vomer.name: Vomer
Cranium/Vomer.description: A thin, unpaired midline bone forming the back and lower part of the nasal septum. It joins the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid above and the septal cartilage in front.

Cranium/Inferior conchae.name: Inferior nasal conchae
Cranium/Inferior conchae.description: Paired scroll-shaped bones on the lateral walls of the nasal cavity. Unlike the superior and middle conchae, which belong to the ethmoid, they are separate bones; the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus beneath each one.

Mandible1/Mandible.name: Mandible
Mandible1/Mandible.description: The lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull. Its condylar processes form the temporomandibular joints, the coronoid processes receive temporalis, and the inferior alveolar nerve runs in the mandibular canal to exit as the mental nerve at the mental foramen.

Cranium/Teeth.name: Upper teeth
Cranium/Teeth.description: The maxillary dental arch, rooted in sockets of the maxillae's alveolar processes (a fibrous gomphosis joint). Each adult quadrant has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars; the upper teeth are supplied by the superior alveolar nerves from the maxillary nerve (V2).

Mandible1/Lower teeth.name: Lower teeth
Mandible1/Lower teeth.description: The mandibular dental arch, rooted in the alveolar part of the mandible. The lower teeth are supplied by the inferior alveolar nerve from the mandibular nerve (V3), which is why an inferior alveolar block numbs one half of the lower jaw.

notes: Bone identities follow the creator's (WitmerLab) object names and were checked in focused renders; left/right follows object names and matches position (left bones at +x). The inferior conchae are one mesh for both sides. Atlas links use side-less names (e.g. 'Parietal bone') because side-specific skull names do not resolve. Bone colour set to the creator's beige; the lacrimal meshes look larger than a typical lacrimal bone and may include a little adjacent orbital wall from segmentation.
